--- title: "Reproducible R Environments with renv :: Cheatsheet" description: " " image-alt: "" execute: eval: true output: false warning: false --- ::: {.cell .column-margin}

::: The **renv** package helps you create isolated, portable, and reproducible environments for your R projects. Use as little or as much of renv as you need -- if all you want is project isolation, then `renv::init()` is all you need. All of the "regular" tools for R package management and installation continue to work with renv. renv works with typical R package repositories (CRAN, Posit Package Manager, R-universe) and common Git services (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket). ## Core Concepts - An R **library** is a directory of installed R packages. When you install a package (e.g. via `install.packages()`), it goes into the first writable library on your `.libPaths()`. - renv projects use an *isolated* **project library**. Installing or removing packages in one renv project does not affect other renv projects, or your default R library. - The **lockfile** (`renv.lock`) records the exact source and version of every package your project uses. `renv::snapshot()` writes it; `renv::restore()` reads it. - The global **package cache** is shared across all of your renv projects. Project libraries are populated with links into the cache, so creating a new project library is cheap, and installing a package you've used before is fast. ## The renv Workflow The core reproducibility loop ties every function together: 1. `renv::init()` -- set up an isolated project library. 2. `renv::install()` / `renv::update()` -- add and update packages as you work. 3. Confirm your code still works, then `renv::snapshot()` -- record the exact package versions to the **lockfile** (`renv.lock`). 4. Commit the project files to version control and share it (see **Collaboration** below). 5. A collaborator (or future you) runs `renv::restore()` to reinstall those exact versions. ## Collaboration Commit these files to version control so collaborators can reproduce your project: - `renv.lock` -- the lockfile of exact package versions. - `.Rprofile` -- activates renv for new R sessions in the project. - `renv/activate.R` -- the activation script. - `renv/settings.json` -- project-level settings. renv writes a `.gitignore` for you so the project library itself is not committed -- you share the lockfile, not the installed packages. When a collaborator opens the project, renv automatically prompts them to run `renv::restore()`. The same workflow powers CI: [`r-lib/actions/setup-renv`](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/tree/v2-branch/setup-renv) restores your lockfile on GitHub Actions; see the [CI vignette](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/ci.html) for other services. ## Getting Started - Call `renv::init()` on a new or existing project to initialize renv. - `renv::init()` creates a project `.Rprofile` and `renv/activate.R`, which automatically activate renv for new R sessions started in the project. - Set project options at init time, e.g. to use explicit snapshots: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} renv::init(settings = list(snapshot.type = "explicit")) ``` ::: ## Install & Update Packages Use these to change *which* packages (and versions) are in your project library: - `renv::install()`: Install one or more named packages. Supports custom remotes, e.g. `renv::install("tidyverse/dplyr")` (GitHub) or a specific version with `renv::install("dplyr@1.1.0")`. With no arguments, installs the packages your project requires. - `renv::update()`: Update packages (all by default, or those you name) to the latest version available from the source they were installed from. - `renv::remove()`: Remove packages from the project library. Enable [pak](https://pak.r-lib.org) for faster, parallel installs with `options(renv.config.pak.enabled = TRUE)`. ## Snapshot & Restore Use these to save and reproduce the *state* of your project library: - `renv::status()`: Check whether your lockfile and library are in sync (see **Staying in Sync**). - `renv::snapshot()`: Save the state of your project library to the lockfile. - `renv::restore()`: Install the exact package versions recorded in the lockfile. - `renv::record()`: Record a specific package version in the lockfile without installing it. ## Staying in Sync `renv::status()` reports when your project is out of sync, and how to fix it: - Packages installed or updated, but not recorded in the lockfile? Record them with `renv::snapshot()`. - Packages recorded in the lockfile, but not installed? Reinstall them with `renv::restore()`. - Packages used in your code, but not installed? Install them with `renv::install()`, then `renv::snapshot()`. - Pulled a collaborator's changes to `renv.lock`? Sync up with `renv::restore()`. When in doubt, treat the lockfile as the source of truth -- your project library can always be rebuilt from it with `renv::restore()`. ## Dependencies `renv::dependencies()`: Discover the packages used in your project's R, R Markdown, and Quarto files. The rmarkdown package is required to scan dependencies in R Markdown and Quarto files. Use a `.renvignore` file to exclude files or directories from dependency discovery, and `renv::settings$ignored.packages()` to keep development-only packages (e.g. devtools) out of the lockfile. renv supports several **snapshot types**, set with `renv::settings$snapshot.type()`. The two most common: | Type | What it captures | |-------------------|-----------------------------------------------------| | `"implicit"` (default) | Scans your files with `renv::dependencies()` (e.g. `library(dplyr)`, `dplyr::mutate()`). | | `"explicit"` | Only packages listed in the project `DESCRIPTION` file, which you maintain. | ## Configuring renv - `?renv::config`: User-specific settings. Tweak how renv behaves in different scenarios. - `?renv::settings`: Project-level settings. Persisted with the project and active for all collaborators. - `renv::deactivate()` / `renv::activate()`: Temporarily turn renv off in a project, and turn it back on. ## Other Useful Functions - `renv::history()` / `renv::revert()`: View past lockfiles from version control, and roll back to an earlier one. - `renv::upgrade()`: Upgrade the version of renv used by the project. - `renv::repair()`: Fix a project library whose links into the global cache have broken (e.g. after moving or cleaning the cache). - `renv::purge()`: Remove packages from the global cache (e.g. to reclaim space or clear a broken install). - `renv::diagnostics()`: Print a diagnostics report; useful for bug reports at [github.com/rstudio/renv](https://github.com/rstudio/renv). ## What renv Does Not Do renv reproduces R packages, not your whole environment. It does not manage: - Your R version -- renv records it in the lockfile and warns on mismatch, but does not install it. Use a tool like [rig](https://github.com/r-lib/rig) to install and switch R versions. - Pandoc -- required to render R Markdown and Quarto documents. - System libraries, the OS, and compiler versions -- for full reproducibility, pair renv with Docker. `renv::restore()` can also fail when a package must be compiled from source and its system prerequisites (or original binaries) are unavailable. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ CC BY SA Posit Software, PBC • [info\@posit.co](mailto:info@posit.co) • [posit.co](https://posit.co) Learn more at [rstudio.github.io/renv](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/) Updated: 2026-08. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} packageVersion("renv") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] '1.2.3' ``` ::: ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------
